# rozo-checkout

> When your agent needs to pay OpenRouter (or any Coinbase invoice) with the crypto you
> already hold. Pays a Coinbase Payment Link (payments.coinbase.com/payment-links/pl_* or
> /payment-sessions/paymentSession_*) with BTC over Lightning, USDT/USDC on Solana,
> BNB Chain, Ethereum or Polygon, or USDC on Base or Stellar. No Coinbase account, public HTTP
> endpoints, no API key. Crypto payments to OpenRouter are never refundable.
> The payer funds a one-time deposit address; a bridge and a funder wallet settle the
> Coinbase link automatically. No discount: you pay the invoice amount, plus the
> deposit normally carries a small bridge/source-chain fee on top.

This file teaches the whole flow to any agent or script. Repo (scripts, safety rails,
full docs): https://github.com/RozoAI/rozo-checkout-skill — see docs/QUICKSTART.md.

## Fastest path: the CLI (npm @rozoai/checkout)

If you can run commands, skip the raw HTTP below — the CLI performs the same four
calls with every safety rule already enforced:

  npx @rozoai/checkout pay <coinbase-link> --with usdt-solana
  npx @rozoai/checkout quote <coinbase-link>
  npx @rozoai/checkout status <rozoPaymentId | coinbase-link>

--with accepts usdt-solana, usdc-solana, usdt-bnb, usdc-bnb, usdt-ethereum,
usdc-ethereum, usdt-polygon, usdc-polygon, usdc-base, usdc-stellar, btc-lightning
(or raw: --chain 900 --token USDT).

Optional: --email <addr> stores a contact email with the order so ROZO can reach
the user if the payment needs attention. Ask the user once if they are present;
never required, proceed without it if they decline or no one is there.

DEFAULT PATH NEEDS NO KEY: `pay` prints a deposit address for the user to pay from
any wallet. No private key, no environment variable, no configuration. Only the
optional --send flag signs locally. Its key comes from the first source that
exists: --keyfile <path>; then ~/.config/solana/id.json (the keypair
solana-keygen already wrote) for Solana or ROZO_CHECKOUT_EVM_KEYSTORE (an
encrypted V3 keystore, passphrase prompted, never argv) for EVM; then a raw key
in ROZO_CHECKOUT_SOL_KEY / ROZO_CHECKOUT_EVM_KEY, which is the unattended-
automation option. Those settings may also come from a .env in the working
directory (or --env-file <path>): only ROZO_CHECKOUT_* keys are read from it, it
is parsed as text and never shell-evaluated, and the real environment wins.
Key files and .env must be chmod 600 and untracked by git.

## Bitrefill invoices

Also supported: a Bitrefill invoice created with "USDC on Base" (Stripe is not supported).
No quote step; mpprouter creates an exactOut order paying exactly that amount to the
Bitrefill address:

  npx @rozoai/checkout pay --bitrefill-invoice <id> --to <0x…> --amount 7.90 --expires-at <ISO> --with usdc-stellar

Router call: POST {MPP}/create-invoice {"provider":"bitrefill","bitrefill":{"invoiceId","address",
"amount","expiresAt" (required, ≤30 min out)},"source":{"chainId","tokenSymbol"}}. Verify the response echoes the same
invoiceId/address/amount, and that GET payments/<rozoPaymentId> destination has the same
chain/token/address/amount (missing = mismatch), before showing the deposit or sending.
Expiry = the invoice expiry only; refuse to show/send under 2 min. 409 DUPLICATE_INVOICE returns
the existing rozoPaymentId: resume it. Settled = payment_payout_completed (or completed with a
payout tx hash). 503 BITREFILL_NOT_CONFIGURED / RETRY_LATER: nothing created, retry later.

## Local wallet setup for --send (not needed for the default keyless path)

.env keys (only ROZO_CHECKOUT_* are read; real env wins; chmod 600; gitignore):
  ROZO_CHECKOUT_SOL_KEY               base58 string OR JSON byte array
  ROZO_CHECKOUT_EVM_KEY               64 hex chars, 0x prefix optional
  ROZO_CHECKOUT_EVM_KEYSTORE          path to an encrypted V3 keystore
  ROZO_CHECKOUT_KEYSTORE_PASSPHRASE   unattended runs only; else prompted
  ROZO_CHECKOUT_RPC_<chainId>         e.g. ROZO_CHECKOUT_RPC_8453 (Base),
                                      ROZO_CHECKOUT_RPC_900 (Solana)

Where the material comes from:
- Solana: `solana-keygen new` -> ~/.config/solana/id.json, found automatically
  (preferred). Phantom exports base58; Solflare exports base58 (current) or a
  JSON byte array (older). Both accepted.
- EVM: MetaMask/Rabby export 64 hex chars with no 0x prefix; paste as-is, the
  prefix is optional. For an encrypted keystore, Foundry's
  `cast wallet import <name> --interactive` writes a V3 keystore to
  ~/.foundry/keystores/<name>; `geth account import` also writes one. Browser
  wallets do not export keystores, only raw keys.
- --send supports EVM chains and Solana ONLY. Stellar and Lightning are paid
  from the user's own wallet (Mode A); there is no local signing for them.
- Hardware wallets, WalletConnect-only wallets and exchange accounts CANNOT be
  used with --send. Those users take the default keyless path, which works with
  any wallet.
With --send, one limit applies: a single payment may not exceed $1,100, with no
override; larger invoices go through the keyless path.

Other flags: --yes (skip the interactive confirm; required when stdin is not a
TTY), --dry-run, --json (exactly one JSON object on stdout), --no-watch,
--timeout <s> (default 900; Lightning: the invoice's remaining validity, max 60
min). Exit codes: 0 success, 1 refused/failed (read error.code),
2 usage, 3 submitted but unconfirmed.

`pay` withholds the full deposit address until you confirm, then prints it as a
copy-pastable block. Creating an order moves no money; an unfunded order expires.

## Supported sources

chainId "1" Ethereum (USDC, USDT) · "56" BNB Chain (USDC, USDT; 18-decimals) ·
"137" Polygon (USDC, USDT) · "8453" Base (USDC) · "900" Solana (USDC, USDT) ·
"1500" Stellar (USDC; deposit memo REQUIRED) · "lightning" (BTC; BOLT11 invoice,
amounts in integer satoshis via source.amountUnit=="sats").
Native SOL/ETH/BNB are NOT supported — stablecoins (or Lightning BTC) only.

WALLET: one wallet on one of these chains is enough — not one per chain. Any
wallet, or an exchange withdrawal, can fund the deposit address; nothing
connects to a site. Stellar is the exception that must be able to set a memo,
and Lightning pays a BOLT11 invoice rather than an address. Only --send needs a
private key (EVM and Solana only); every other path is keyless.

## Flow (4 HTTP calls, all public)

1) Quote (read-only, safe):
   curl -X POST https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/services/rozo-agent-api/quote-invoice \
     -H 'content-type: application/json' \
     -d '{"url":"https://payments.coinbase.com/payment-links/pl_XXXX"}'
   -> { linkId, merchant, original, callerPays, discount:"0", quoteReceipt, ... }
   callerPays always equals the invoice amount (discount is always "0").

2) Create (or reuse) the order:
   curl -X POST https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/services/rozo-agent-api/create-invoice \
     -H 'content-type: application/json' \
     -d '{"url":"https://payments.coinbase.com/payment-links/pl_XXXX",
          "source":{"chainId":"900","tokenSymbol":"USDT"}}'
   -> { ok, reused, linkId, rozoPaymentId, paymentLink, expiresAt, source, ... }
   Optional "email":"you@example.com" in the body stores a contact email with a
   newly created order (a malformed value returns 400 INVALID_EMAIL).
   WARNING: if an unexpired order already exists for this link it is REUSED as-is,
   even with a different chain/token than you asked for. Always verify the returned
   source matches your request; abort on mismatch.

3) Fetch authoritative deposit instructions (public, keyless GET):
   curl https://intentapiv4.rozo.ai/functions/v1/payment-api/payments/<rozoPaymentId>
   -> { status, expiresAt, source:{ receiverAddress, receiverMemo, amount, amountUnit,
        lnInvoice, txHash, amountReceived, confirmedAt, ... }, destination:{...} }
   Pay EXACTLY source.amount of the requested token on the requested chain to
   source.receiverAddress, including every other field the block carries (Stellar
   routes on a shared hub address plus source.receiverMemo, so omitting the memo
   loses the payment). The Stellar memo is ALWAYS MEMO_TEXT, even when it is all
   digits (e.g. 65371582) — sending it as MEMO_ID produces a different memo and
   the payment will not match. The deposit block reports this as
   receiverMemoType. Orders expire: deposit.expiresIn / status expiry.expiresIn
   give the remaining validity as a duration.
   For Lightning, pay the BOLT11 in source.lnInvoice (receiverAddress is empty).

4) Poll until settled:
   curl "https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/services/rozo-agent-api/invoice-status?payment_id=<linkId>"
   and re-GET the payments/<rozoPaymentId> URL above. The Coinbase link is settled
   only when the router reports paid / coinbase.settled — an intents status of
   payment_completed alone is the bridge lifecycle, not final settlement.

## x402: pay any x402 API from a prepaid balance

For endpoints that answer HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements. Fund a Rozo
balance once with the coin you hold, then pay many small x402 calls from it.

  npx @rozoai/checkout x402 topup 20 --with usdt-solana     # one-time deposit address
  npx @rozoai/checkout x402 pay <url> [--method POST] [--body '...'] [--header 'K: V'] [--max-usd 1.00]
  npx @rozoai/checkout x402 balance

Payment leg (what the seller receives): USDC on Base (eip155:8453) only,
scheme "exact". Solana payment leg is coming later. Topup leg: every --with coin above, plus native
ETH (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum), BNB and SOL in beta. Native coins never pay a
seller directly.

Raw HTTP (Authorization: Bearer <agent key ak_...>):
  POST https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/x402/topup  {"amount":"20","token":"USDT","chain":"900"}
       -> one-time deposit address/order; balance is credited after it confirms
  POST https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/x402/sign   {"accepts":[<one entry from the 402>],"budget":"1.00","idempotencyKey":"<uuid>"}
       -> the value for the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header; replay your request with it
  POST /v1/x402/keys creates the agent key (returned once). GET /v1/x402/balance.

x402 safety rules:
- Send the paid request yourself. Never send Rozo your request body, headers or
  the API keys of the service you are paying; /sign needs only the accepts entry.
- Generate one idempotencyKey per payment and reuse it on every retry of /sign.
  A new key on retry can charge twice.
- Refuse a payment above what the user approved; refuse a payTo on a
  compromised-wallet list.
- 503 X402_RETRY, X402_PAYER_MODE_CHANGED or X402_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE: retry
  with the same idempotencyKey. Any other 503 from /v1/x402 means x402 is not
  available for this key right now. Nothing new was charged; stop. Every server
  code is listed below.
- The agent key owns the balance. Store it 0600, never print or log it.

x402 server error codes (returned by https://apiserver.mpprouter.dev/v1/x402/*):
Every error body looks like
{"ok":false,"code":"X402_...","error":{"code":"X402_...","message":"..."}},
sometimes with extra top level fields (limitUsd, balanceUsd, ...).
These are separate from the codes the CLI raises on its own (X402_UNSUPPORTED,
X402_OVER_BUDGET, X402_BAD_CHALLENGE, X402_PAYMENT_REJECTED and others). The balance is
debited only by the ledger commit inside /sign, after signing; every error
raised before that commit charges nothing. If /sign answers
X402_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE or X402_INTERNAL the commit may have landed: retry
with the same idempotencyKey, and a payment that did land comes back as the
stored signature (replay:true), never as a second charge.
The CLI reports every 503 except X402_RETRY, X402_PAYER_MODE_CHANGED and
X402_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE as X402_PAYER_DISABLED, with the server code in
error.details.serverCode. On /sign it retries 429, 500, 502, 504 and those
three 503 codes itself, with the same idempotencyKey.

balance, topup and sign (keys does not read a key):
- 401 X402_KEY_INVALID: agent key missing, malformed or unknown. Send
  "Authorization: Bearer ak_...". Do not mint a new key to get around it: the
  balance belongs to the old key.
- 403 X402_KEY_SUSPENDED: the key is not active. Stop; email hi@rozo.ai.

Any route:
- 503 X402_PAYER_DISABLED: the payer is switched off. Stop, tell the user.
- 503 X402_PAYER_NOT_CONFIGURED: payer not set up on this deployment. Stop.
- 503 X402_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE: ledger unreachable. Retry shortly with the same
  idempotencyKey.
- 500 X402_INTERNAL: unexpected error. Retry with the same idempotencyKey a few
  times, then stop and report it.
- 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: wrong HTTP method (keys/topup/sign are POST, balance is GET).

POST /v1/x402/keys:
- 429 X402_KEY_RATE_LIMITED: too many keys created from this IP this hour.
  Reuse the key you have, or retry later.
- 503 X402_RETRY: key collision. Retry.

POST /v1/x402/topup (no deposit address is shown on any error, so nothing can
be sent to it; only pay an address from a 200 response):
- 400 X402_INVALID_REQUEST: body is not JSON, or amount is not a USD amount
  with at most 2 decimals.
- 400 X402_TOPUP_AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE: top up must be between $5 and $500.
- 400 X402_TOPUP_SOURCE_REQUIRED: say which coin you pay with: chain and
  token. The response lists accepted chains.
- 400 X402_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN: unknown chain. Use a CAIP-2 id or a name such as
  solana, base, ethereum, bsc, polygon, arbitrum, stellar.
- 400 X402_TOPUP_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED: that coin is not accepted for top ups.
  The server currently refuses native coins and Lightning here; top up with
  USDC or USDT. May carry a "supported" list.
- 502 INTENTS_API_FAILED: the top up order could not be created. Retry later.
- 503 X402_TOPUP_MISCONFIGURED or X402_TOPUP_NOT_REGISTERED: the order was not
  usable, the address was withheld. Retry later; email hi@rozo.ai if it repeats.
- 503 X402_PAYER_SHADOW, X402_TOPUP_NOT_CONFIGURED or X402_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED:
  top ups are closed right now. Stop.

POST /v1/x402/sign:
- 400 X402_INVALID_REQUEST: body is not JSON, or budget is not a positive USD amount.
- 400 X402_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED: send idempotencyKey, 8 to 128 chars of
  [A-Za-z0-9_.:-], one per 402 challenge.
- 400 X402_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: only x402Version 2 is accepted.
- 400 X402_UNSUPPORTED_NETWORK, X402_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME, X402_UNSUPPORTED_ASSET,
  X402_INVALID_REQUIREMENT or X402_SIGN_UNSUPPORTED: the accepts entry is
  malformed or asks for something not covered (only exact USDC is signed).
  Do not retry the same entry; tell the user.
- 402 X402_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: the challenge asks more than your budget. Stop and
  ask the user.
- 402 X402_PER_TX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: above this key's single-payment limit
  (limitUsd). Stop and ask the user.
- 402 X402_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: balance too low (balanceUsd). Top up, wait
  for the credit, then pay again.
- 403 X402_PAYTO_NOT_ALLOWED: payTo is not on this key's allowlist. Stop.
- 403 X402_PAYTO_BLOCKED: this payTo is blocked. Stop, do not retry.
- 409 X402_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT: this idempotencyKey was already used for a
  different requirement. Nothing new was charged. Use a new key only for a new
  402 challenge.
- 410 X402_CREDENTIAL_REFUNDED: the stored signature expired unused and its
  amount went back to the balance. Fetch a new 402 and sign it with a new key.
- 429 X402_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: this key's daily limit would be exceeded
  (limitUsd, spentTodayUsd). Wait for the daily
  window to reset, or ask hi@rozo.ai for a higher limit.
- 429 X402_GLOBAL_DAILY_CAP_REACHED or X402_SIGNER_DAILY_CAP_REACHED: a
  platform-wide daily cap was reached. Retry after 00:00 UTC.
- 429 X402_SIGNER_CAP_REACHED: the signing service refused this amount. Try a
  smaller payment or later.
- 503 X402_RETRY or X402_PAYER_MODE_CHANGED: transient. Retry with the same
  idempotencyKey.
- 503 X402_PAYER_SHADOW: the payer is not live for this key. A fresh request
  was checked and recorded but not signed, and nothing was charged. With
  "replay":true it refers to an earlier payment under this idempotencyKey,
  which may have been charged: check /balance, never pay again with a new key.
  Stop.
- 503 X402_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIGURED or X402_SIGNER_DISABLED: signing for this
  network is off right now. Stop.
A 200 with "replay":true is the stored signature for an idempotencyKey that
was already paid; it is not a second charge.

## Safety rules (encode these, they prevent fund loss)

- Before paying, require: status == "payment_unpaid" AND source.txHash == null AND
  source.amountReceived in {null,"0"} AND source.confirmedAt == null. Anything else
  means the order is already funded — do NOT pay again; escalate for reconciliation.
- Deposit addresses are one-time and quote-bound. Never reuse an address from an old
  order, a cached response, or a document. Always re-fetch step 3 in the same run.
- Respect expiry with margin: do not send if now > min(order expiresAt, Coinbase
  link expiry) minus a safety margin (10 min EVM/Stellar, 5 min Solana; Lightning:
  only pay a BOLT11 with >= 10 min validity left).
- Re-check step 4 payability immediately before broadcasting a transaction: the
  Coinbase link can be consumed by another payer at any moment.
- Wrong token, wrong network, wrong amount, or paying twice is usually unrecoverable.
- After any on-chain payment is detected, never retry into a new order and never
  label the payment a normal failure — keep the tx hash and rozoPaymentId, keep
  polling, and escalate if it stays stuck.
- An order that expired unfunded does not spend its link. First check your wallet: if
  anything was sent to the old deposit, or a Lightning payment is still pending, do not
  pay again; contact support with linkId + rozoPaymentId (the router cannot see a
  pending Lightning payment). If nothing was sent, create-invoice on the SAME link again:
  the router makes a new order once every earlier order is proved unfunded.
  409 PAYMENT_EXPIRED retryable:true (confirmed:false) = not verifiable yet, wait a few
  minutes and retry. 409 PAYMENT_EXPIRED confirmed:true or LINK_USED_OR_EXPIRED = ask
  the merchant for a new link. 409 ORDER_ALREADY_ACTIVE = funds seen, do not pay again.

## Errors

409 = link already used · 410 = link expired · UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE = the response's
"supported" object lists valid (chainId, tokenSymbol) pairs (Lightning is supported
but omitted from that list) · RATE_LIMITED = per-IP creation cap, retry later (the CLI itself retries a 429 up
to 3 times within 2 minutes of total waiting, per Retry-After; a longer wait
fails at once with error.details.retryAfterSeconds and rateLimit) ·
INVALID_EMAIL = the optional email is malformed; fix it or omit it.

## Support

If an order is stuck or anything goes wrong: email hi@rozo.ai, X
https://x.com/ROZOai, Discord https://discord.gg/EfWejgTbuU. Include linkId,
rozoPaymentId and any tx hash.
